body:
If your vape sounds like a straw at the bottom of a drink, a bubbling, crackling gurgle every time you inhale, liquid is where it should not be. Gurgling is annoying, it makes the vapor taste wet and can lead to spit-back, where hot droplets reach your mouth, and it is almost always fixable. This guide explains why a vape gurgles, how to clear it step by step, how to stop it coming back, how the problem differs in pods, tanks and disposables, what worn parts can cause it, how liquid type and airflow play a part and what to do if the sound will not go away. It is written for adults aged 21 and over. Nicotine is addictive.

## Why it gurgles
Excess liquid has pooled in the airflow channel or around the coil, often from overfilling, a flooded coil or a faulty seal. When you inhale, air passes through the liquid and bubbles, which makes the sound. The extra liquid can also reach the coil, where it spits as it heats. A little noise from a freshly filled tank is normal for the first puff or two, but a continuing gurgle is a sign that something is wrong.

### The mechanics
Inside a tank or pod, liquid should reach the coil only through the wick. Air should pass through the airflow channel without touching liquid. If liquid gets into the channel, air bubbles through it. The channel may be flooded by overfilling, by liquid that is too thin, by a coil that is not wicking properly or by a gap in a seal.

## Fix it step by step
1. Remove the pod or tank and wipe the outside.
2. Blow gently through the mouthpiece with the coil facing down, so excess liquid drains out through the airflow. Do this over a paper towel.
3. Wipe the contacts and the airflow holes with a dry cotton bud.
4. Let it sit upright for several minutes before using it again.
5. Take a few dry puffs without pressing the button, if your device allows, to clear the channel.
6. Refill below the max line, and avoid splashing liquid down the center.
7. Test with gentle puffs, then normal ones.

If the sound is gone, you are done. If it returns, move on to the causes below.

## Prevent it
- **Do not overfill.** Fill below the line, not to the top.
- **Avoid very thin liquid in large-coil tanks.** It floods the coil.
- **Open airflow slightly** if it keeps happening, because tight airflow with a loose coil can make liquid condense.
- **Keep devices upright** when not in use.
- **Prime new coils properly,** but do not oversaturate them.
- **Let the device rest** after filling, so liquid settles.

## Worn parts
A cracked pod, damaged seal or worn coil can cause recurrent flooding. Replace them. See [how often to replace coils](/blog/how-often-to-replace-coils/) and [leaks and fixes](/blog/vape-leaking-causes-and-fixes/). If the gurgle began after a drop, look for cracks. If it began after many weeks of use, suspect the coil.

## Liquid and airflow
The balance between liquid thickness and airflow matters. Thin, high-PG liquid flows easily and can flood a coil with big wicking holes. Thick, high-VG liquid wicks slowly and can leave the coil starved, then flooded as it catches up. Match liquid to hardware; see [PG and VG ratios](/blog/pg-vg-ratio-explained/). Airflow that is very open can cause condensation to collect, and airflow that is very tight can build pressure.

## Gurgling by device type
### Pods
Gurgling in a pod usually comes from overfilling or a pod that has not seated properly. Remove it, drain the airflow, refill below the line and click it in firmly.

### Tanks
Tanks have more places for liquid to collect. Check the coil is screwed in tightly, the O-rings are in place and the tank is not overfilled. Check the airflow control and open it a little.

### Disposables
Gurgling in a disposable usually means condensation. Hold it upright for a minute and draw gently. If it persists, the device may have a fault, or liquid may have pooled during shipping or storage. Do not try to open it. Contact us if it is new and does not stop.

## What about spit-back?
Spit-back, hot droplets reaching your mouth, often accompanies gurgling, because liquid reaches the hot coil and boils. It stops when the flooding stops. Follow the steps above, and take gentler puffs. See [vape spitting or hot vapor fixes](/blog/vape-spitting-or-hot-vapor-fixes/).

## Cleaning the airflow channel
If the airflow channel is dirty, it can hold liquid. For refillable tanks, rinse the parts that can be rinsed with warm water, dry them fully and reassemble. Do not wet the battery or electronics. For pods, wipe the visible parts, and do not rinse the coil. See [how to clean a vape device](/blog/how-to-clean-a-vape-device/).

## What not to do
- **Do not keep vaping through heavy gurgling.** It spits hot liquid and wastes the coil.
- **Do not shake the device to clear it.** It can force liquid further in.
- **Do not use compressed air at high pressure** on the coil or the sensor.
- **Do not open a sealed disposable.**

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Why does my vape gurgle right after filling?
You may have overfilled or splashed liquid into the airflow. Drain it and let it rest.

### Does a gurgle mean the coil is dead?
Not necessarily. Flooding often clears with the steps above. If it keeps coming back with a fresh fill, check the coil and the seals.

### Is gurgling the same as a leak?
They are related, because both come from liquid in the wrong place. A leak escapes the device. A gurgle stays inside the airflow.

### Can a cold day cause gurgling?
Cold thickens liquid and can change wicking. Let the device warm to room temperature.

### How long should I wait after clearing it?
A few minutes upright is usually enough. If you primed a new coil, wait longer.

## Replace
Browse [coils and pods](/shop/coils-pods/) for replacement parts. See also [why a vape is not hitting](/blog/why-is-my-vape-not-hitting/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## Case studies
### The gurgle after a fresh fill
A customer filled their tank to the top and tilted it badly, so liquid ran into the center tube. The first puffs gurgled. Draining the airflow and refilling slowly below the line fixed it. Lesson: how you fill matters as much as how much.

### The gurgle that kept returning
A tank gurgled every few days. The cause was an O-ring that had hardened. A new O-ring fixed it. Lesson: when a fix does not last, suspect a worn part.

### The gurgle in a large-coil tank
A thin liquid in a big sub-ohm coil flooded it repeatedly. Switching to a higher-VG liquid, and closing the airflow a little, solved the problem. Lesson: match liquid to coil.

## Tools that help
A cotton bud for wiping contacts, paper towels for draining and a small brush for the airflow openings are all you need. Keep them with your device, and clear problems early, before they spread liquid further into the device.

## How to tell flooding from a worn coil
Flooding usually clears with draining and resting, and a fresh fill with care avoids it. A worn coil gives flat flavor even with the right amount of liquid, and a new coil restores it. If you cannot tell which it is, try a new coil. If the gurgle returns with a new coil, the seals or the liquid are the cause.

## A note on spitting and popping
Gurgling is often followed by a spitting or popping sound as droplets hit the hot coil. It is unpleasant, and it can burn the wick. Take it seriously, stop vaping and clear the device, because continued use wears the coil quickly.

## Frequently asked questions about noise
### Is a crackling sound the same as gurgling?
Crackling often comes from liquid on a hot coil, and gurgling from liquid in the airflow. They have similar causes. Clear the device and check the liquid level.

### Why does my disposable gurgle when new?
Liquid can move during shipping and settle. Hold it upright for a few minutes, and draw gently. If it continues, contact us.

### Does gurgling mean I filled it wrong?
Often yes. Fill slowly, below the line, and keep liquid away from the center tube.

### Can I prevent gurgling in a pod?
Fill carefully, seat the pod firmly and keep the device upright. Avoid very thin liquid in pods designed for thick liquid.

## A final troubleshooting summary
If your device gurgles, work through the likely causes in order: first the liquid level and how you filled it, then the airflow channel, then the coil, then the seals and finally the liquid thickness. Change one thing at a time, and test after each change, so that you know what worked. Keep a note of what fixed it, because the same problem tends to recur until the habit that caused it changes. Most gurgling is fixed in minutes with a little patience, and a spare coil or pod on hand means you are never without a working device for long.

## When to contact us
If a device you bought from us gurgles from new and the steps above do not help, contact us through the [contact page](/contact/) with your order ID and a short description or video. We will tell you what applies under our [refund policy](/refunds/), and we will help you decide whether it is a fault or a matter of setup.
